extracted.intended_audience: Patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) filing and prosecuting U.S. patent applications before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, prosecuting, abandoning, reviving, and obtaining design/plant/reissue patents before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Covers interview practice, reply deadlines, extensions, restriction/joinder, and special rules for design/plant/reissue filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews location and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours, as the respective examiners may designate. Interviews will not be permitted at any other time or place without the authority of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may designate specific premises/hours; Director authorization required for off‑premises or off‑hours interviews. (See § 1.133(a)(1).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of interview on patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview for the discussion of the patentability of a pending application will not occur before the first Office action, unless the application is a continuing or substitute application or the examiner determines that such an interview would advance prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews on patentability generally occur after the first Office action unless one of the specified exceptions applies. (See § 1.133(a)(2).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may require that an interview be scheduled in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be prepared to schedule interviews in advance when requested by the examiner. (See § 1.133(a)(3).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement after interview for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview with an examiner, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview does not remove the necessity for reply to Office actions as specified in §§ 1.111 and 1.135. File a full written statement capturing interview arguments when requesting reconsideration. (See § 1.133(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for reply to an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office action will notify the applicant of any non‑statutory or shortened statutory time period set for reply to an Office action. Unless the applicant is notified in writing that a reply is required in less than six months, a maximum period of six months is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default maximum reply period is six months unless a shorter in‑writing period is set. (See § 1.134.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant of a patent application fails to reply within the time period provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file an appropriate reply causes abandonment. (See § 1.135(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to save prosecution from abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution of an application to save it from abandonment pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section must include such complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bona fide attempt that substantially replies to a non‑final Office action but omits some matter may, under limited circumstances, be permitted to supply the omission with a new time period. Amendments after final rejection or amendments not responsive to the last action generally will not save the application. (See § 1.135(b)–(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time period for reply up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply, if a petition for an extension of time and the fee set in § 1.17(a) or (u) are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions require timely petition and payment of the specified fee; availability is limited by statute maximums. The date the petition and fee are filed determines the extension period and fee. (See § 1.136(a)(1)–(2).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time — situations where not available
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions under § 1.136(a) are not available where: (i) applicant is notified otherwise in an Office action; (ii) reply is a reply brief under § 41.41; (iii) reply is a request for oral hearing under § 41.47(a); (iv) reply is to certain PTAB decisions (§ 41.50, § 41.52, § 90.3); or (v) the application is involved in a contested case or derivation proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check exception list before filing for an extension; where exceptions apply, § 1.136(a) extensions cannot be used. (See § 1.136(a)(1)(i)–(v).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive petitions and authorization to charge fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request may be submitted authorizing any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for an extension to be treated as incorporating a petition for the appropriate length of time, and authorization to charge required fees will be treated as a constructive petition for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the fee may be treated as a constructive petition for extension for concurrent replies; plan fee payments accordingly. (See § 1.136(a)(3).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for sufficient cause (paragraph b)
rubrics_metrics.description: When paragraph (a) provisions are not available, the period for reply will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; any request must be filed on or before the day reply is due and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere filing of the request does not effect an extension; it must show sufficient cause. No extension can exceed the statute maximum. (See § 1.136(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑extendable periods after Notice of Allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is notified in a 'Notice of Allowability' that an application is otherwise in condition for allowance, the following time periods are not extendable if set in the Notice of Allowability or in an Office action having a mail date on or after the mail date of the Notice of Allowability: (1) the period for submitting the inventor’s oath or declaration; (2) the period for submitting formal drawings set under § 1.85(c); and (3) the period for making a deposit set under § 1.809(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a Notice of Allowability issues, certain allowance-related deadlines cannot be extended. (See § 1.136(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of abandoned application for unintentional delay
rubrics_metrics.description: If the delay in reply by applicant or patent owner was unintentional, a petition may be filed to revive an abandoned application or a reexamination prosecution terminated or limited, pursuant to § 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival is available only where delay was unintentional; follow petition requirements exactly. (See § 1.137(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements to revive (unintentional delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition to revive must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee as set in § 1.17(m); (3) any terminal disclaimer (and fee) required under paragraph (d); and (4) a statement that the entire delay in filing the required reply was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may require additional information. Failure to include required items will render petition non‑grantable. (See § 1.137(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply contents to revive various abandonment types
rubrics_metrics.description: For abandonment under § 1.57(a), reply must include copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application. For abandonment for failure to pay issue or publication fee, reply must include payment. For abandonment for failure to prosecute, required reply may be filing a continuing application; for nonprovisional utility or plant abandoned after close of prosecution, filing an RCE in compliance with § 1.114 may also meet the reply requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required revival reply depends on the reason for abandonment; include documents/payments or continuation/RCE as appropriate. (See § 1.137(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement for revival
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition to revive in a design application must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer dedicating to the public a terminal part of the term of any patent granted thereon equivalent to the period of abandonment. For utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, revival petitions must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer dedicating a terminal portion of term equivalent to the lesser of (i) period of abandonment, or (ii) period extending beyond twenty years from the earliest-filed application date; additional rules apply to continuing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer requirements depend on application type and filing date; certain exceptions exist (e.g., revival solely for copendency with later-filed apps, reissue, reexamination). (See § 1.137(d)(1)–(3).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration of refusal to revive — timing and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive must be filed within two months of the decision refusing to revive or within such time as set in the decision. Unless indicated otherwise, this period may be extended under provisions for abandoned applications and relevant reexamination or PTAB rules as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file reconsideration requests; applicable extension provisions vary by proceeding type. (See § 1.137(e) and cross‑references.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival for failure to notify Office of foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application abandoned pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii) for failure to timely notify the Office of the filing of an application in a foreign country or multinational treaty may be revived; the reply requirement is met by the notification, but revival petition will not stay any running reply periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of the foreign filing satisfies the reply portion, but revival does not halt other deadlines. (See § 1.137(f).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of provisional applications and provisional pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application abandoned for failure to timely respond to an Office requirement may be revived pursuant to § 1.137. Subject to 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3) and § 1.7(b), a provisional application will not be regarded as pending after twelve months from its filing date under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional revival possible, but pendency only lasts twelve months; plan filings accordingly. (See § 1.137(g).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration of abandonment identifying the application in the USPTO. The declaration must be signed by a party authorized under § 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(3) to sign a paper in the application, except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express abandonment takes effect when received by appropriate officials in time to act; signature and authorization requirements apply. (See § 1.138(a)–(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment to avoid publication — petition and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking to abandon an application to avoid publication must submit a declaration of express abandonment by way of a petition including the fee in § 1.17(h) in sufficient time to permit officials to recognize the abandonment and remove the application from publication. Applicants should expect petition will not be granted and must file more than four weeks prior to the projected date of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on last‑minute petitions to avoid publication; petition likely denied if late. (See § 1.138(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for refund of search/excess claims fees — timing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking to abandon an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or § 1.53(b) on or after Dec. 8, 2004, or a national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 to obtain a refund of the search fee and excess claims fee must submit a declaration of express abandonment by petition before an examination has been made; refunds are limited to the fees listed in §§ 1.16 and 1.492 and if refund request is not filed with the declaration or within two months the Office may retain the fees. The two‑month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File refund‑seeking abandonment petitions before examination and within two months to preserve refund eligibility. (See § 1.138(d).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder: prohibition on claiming independent distinct inventions in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more independent and distinct inventions may not be claimed in one national application, except that more than one species of an invention, not to exceed a reasonable number, may be claimed provided the application also includes an allowable generic claim and extra species claims are in dependent form or include all limitations of the generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not claim separate, patentably distinct inventions in one application; use divisional/continuing applications or proper dependent/species structure when a genus exists. (See § 1.141(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑category claims and three‑way restriction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims to product, process of making, and process of use are included, a three‑way requirement for restriction can only be made where the process of making is distinct from the product. If process of making and the product are not distinct, the process of using may be joined with claims directed to the product and the process of making even though distinctness between product and process of using can be shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction practice among product/process/use categories depends on distinctness relationships; examiners must apply distinctness analysis before imposing a three‑way restriction. (See § 1.141(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for restriction (election) procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more independent and distinct inventions are claimed in a single application, the examiner will require the applicant in the reply to elect an invention to which the claims will be restricted (requirement for restriction). Such requirement will normally be made before any action on the merits, but may be made at any time before final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When faced with a restriction requirement, elect an invention for prosecution in the reply; non‑elected claims are withdrawn from further consideration but may be reinstated if the requirement is withdrawn or overruled. (See § 1.142(a)–(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent presentation of claims directed to different invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If after an Office action the applicant presents claims directed to an invention distinct from and independent of the previously claimed invention, the applicant will be required to restrict the claims to the invention previously claimed if the amendment is entered, subject to reconsideration and review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments adding distinct inventions after Office action will generally trigger restriction to the earlier elected invention; use reconsideration/appeal routes if disagreeing. (See § 1.145.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of restriction requirement — provisional election
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disagrees with the requirement for restriction, he may request reconsideration and withdrawal or modification of the requirement, giving reasons. In requesting reconsideration the applicant must indicate a provisional election of one invention for prosecution, which will be the election if the requirement becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve prosecution options while seeking reconsideration, make a provisional election and present reasons for withdrawal or modification. (See § 1.143 and § 1.146.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent drawing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The design must be represented by a drawing that complies with § 1.84 and must contain a sufficient number of views to constitute a complete disclosure of the appearance of the design. Appropriate surface shading should be used; solid black surface shading is not permitted except to represent color black. Broken lines may show visible environmental structure but not hidden planes; alternate positions illustrated by full and broken lines in same view are not permitted. Photographs and ink drawings may not be combined; photographs used in lieu of ink drawings must be limited to the design and not disclose environmental structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design drawings must clearly disclose the ornamental appearance without improper use of broken lines, combined media, or excessive environmental detail. Color drawings/photos permitted in limited circumstances. (See § 1.152.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent title, claim and oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the design must designate the particular article. No description other than reference to the drawing is ordinarily required. The claim shall be in formal terms to the ornamental design for the article as shown, or as shown and described. More than one claim is neither required nor permitted. The inventor’s oath or declaration must comply with § 1.63 (or § 1.64 substitute statement where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications are single-claim filings; ensure title names the article and the claim is strictly to the ornamental design as depicted. (See § 1.153.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and content order for design application elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of a design application should appear in order: transmittal form, fee transmittal, application data sheet, specification, drawings or photographs, and inventor’s oath or declaration. The specification should include preamble, cross‑reference to related apps, statement re: federally sponsored research, description of figures, feature description, and a single claim, each section headed in uppercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prescribed element order and section headings to present a complete design application. (See § 1.154.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination for design applications — qualification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for expedited examination the application must include drawings in compliance with § 1.84 (or be an international design application published per Hague Article 10(3)), the applicant must have conducted a preexamination search, and must file a request including the fee (§ 1.17(k)) and a statement that a preexamination search was conducted indicating the field of search and an information disclosure statement in compliance with § 1.98. The Office will not examine an application that is not in condition for examination even if an expedited request is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet all formal drawing, search, fee, and IDS requirements to request expedited examination; ensure the application is otherwise in condition for examination. (See § 1.155.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent — inventor and oath requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor named for a plant patent application must be the person who has invented or discovered and asexually reproduced the new and distinct variety of plant. The inventor’s oath or declaration, in addition to § 1.63 or § 1.64 averments, must state that the inventor has asexually reproduced the plant; for a newly found plant, the oath must state it was found in a cultivated area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patents require specific reproductive and discovery averments in the oath/declaration; only those who asexually reproduced (or as provided in §§ 1.42, 1.43, 1.47) may be applicants. (See § 1.162.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent specification content and order
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain as full and complete a disclosure as possible of the plant and characteristics that distinguish it over related varieties, its antecedents, and must particularly point out where and how the variety has been asexually reproduced. The application elements should appear in an ordered list (transmittal, fees, ADS, specification, drawings, oath), and the specification should include title, cross‑references, federally sponsored research statement, Latin genus/species name, variety denomination, background, summary, drawing description, detailed botanical description, a single claim, and an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed botanical disclosure and follow the required element and section order; include variety denomination and Latin names where applicable. (See § 1.163.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent claim and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim shall be in formal terms to the new and distinct variety of the specified plant as described and illustrated and may recite principal distinguishing characteristics. More than one claim is not permitted. Plant drawings should be artistically and competently executed complying with § 1.84; drawings must disclose all distinctive characteristics capable of visual representation. Drawings may be in color and must be in color if color is a distinguishing characteristic; two copies of color drawings or photographs must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patents are single-claim filings; ensure drawings and description visually disclose distinguishing features and submit color copies when color distinguishes. (See §§ 1.164–1.165.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant specimens and examination cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may be required to furnish specimens of the plant, flower, or fruit in specified quantity and growth stage for study and inspection; if not possible, plants must be made available for official inspection where grown. Applications may be submitted to the Department of Agriculture for study and report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide physical specimens or inspection access if requested and to cooperate with interagency examination. (See §§ 1.166–1.167.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reissue must contain the same parts required for an application for an original patent, complying with all the same rules except as otherwise provided, and in addition comply with rules relating to reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare reissue applications with the same completeness as an original filing and follow specialized reissue rules. (See § 1.171.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applicant and assignee consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue applicant is the original patentee, or the current patent owner if there has been an assignment. A reissue application must be accompanied by the written consent of all assignees currently owning an undivided interest in the patent; assignees consenting must establish ownership by filing submissions in accordance with § 3.73(c). A reissue will be granted to the original patentee, his legal representatives or assigns as the interest may appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper party status and obtain/witness assignee consents and ownership evidence as required when filing a reissue application. (See § 1.172.)
